newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan increases rice support prices.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan increases rice support prices.

text.p: Pakistani authorities on Tuesday increased the official support prices for paddy by 16.10 to 21.42 percent.

A government statement issued after a meeting of the Economic Coordination Committee of the cabinet said the support prices, which the government must pay to producers for the various varieties of paddy from the new 1997/98 crop, had been increased to provide support to rice production.
Rice is one of Pakistan's major export items and the increase in paddy support prices will also reflect in domestic rice prices, market sources said.
Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif's government increased wheat support price earlier this year, leading to increases in flour prices that sparked protests.
On Tuesday, the support price for Pakistan's top Super Basmati variety paddy was set for the first time at 360 rupees ($8.47) for a unit of 40 kg.

Other varities, whose rates were increased: Basmati-385 to 310 rupees from 255.30, IRRI-6 (FAQ) to 153 from 128.00, IRRI-6 (Superior), KS-282, DR-82, DR-83 and DR-92 to 167 from 142.60, and KS-282, DR-82, DR-83 and DR-92 (Superior) to 180.25 from 155.25.
